title: Component provenance stamps & auto-layout normalization for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: Reduce library drift and publishing friction by stamping each component with provenance metadata and enforcing a normalized set of auto-layout constraints for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts. This ticket focuses on three complementary areas: (1) embed structured provenance into the Figma component 'Description' field (token version, owner, last-compat-check, compatible runtime variants), (2) normalize auto-layout anchor settings and min-content rules across atomic components to prevent unintended resizing in responsive containers, (3) consolidate a small set of semantic elevation and spacing tokens referenced by components and document migration steps for teams. Outcome: fewer accidental visual regressions, faster publish reviews, and a lightweight gating step in the publish pipeline that can be automated.
acceptance_criteria: Every core button, table, chart, and token primitive in the team library has a provenance stamp in the Figma component Description that includes: token-set:vX, owner:<name>, last-compat:<YYYY-MM-DD>, notes:<short>.

Auto-layout anchors standardized: horizontal anchors set to 'hug' where appropriate, vertical growth rules set to 'fixed' for buttons and 'fill' for table rows; min-content padding constraints applied to prevent collapse.
Three semantic elevation tokens created (surface-1/surface-2/overlay) and mapped to existing shadow layers in 90%+ occurrences in components.

Design QA checklist added to library publish flow and validated with a canary publish to the 'design-staging' team library without visual regressions on key pages (login, dashboard, table-heavy report).
A lightweight linter rule (JSON manifest check) flags components missing a provenance stamp; PRs must fix or provide justification before publish approval.
tasks: Audit current team library: create spreadsheet of components missing provenance + inconsistent auto-layout settings (expected ~120 components).
Define provenance schema and a short template for the Description field; share with Design + Dev for feedback.
Batch-apply auto-layout fixes for atomic tokens and button components (padding normalization: 12/16 system), document before/after screenshots.
Map shadow layers to three semantic elevation tokens and update token names in the library; ensure token aliasing for backwards compatibility.
Update library publish checklist in Confluence and add a gating lint that validates Description stamps and auto-layout flags.
Run canary publish to 'design-staging' and coordinate visual QA with PM and a front-end engineer; log any regressions and roll back changes if severity is high.
Open GitHub PR with migration plan and update release notes for ui-library-2026.03.
